# Reading Data

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(gridExtra)

```

Working dataframe = mpg (found in ggplot2: variables e.g., displ,, hwy, model, year etc.))

```{r}

ggplot(data = mpg) + #define what dataset to use in the plot
  geom_point(mapping = aes(x = displ, y = hwy)) #basic scatter plot, aes = define what variables to map x,y

# ggplot (data = <DATA>) +
#   <GEOM_FUNCTION> (mapping = aes (<MAPPINGS>))
# Functions : point, map, boxplot, dotplot etc. 
# Aes : size, shape, fill, colour 

```

```{r}

#AES Change colour (colour) by class/scale_colour_gradient or define colour = "green" or HEXcode "#00abff") *outside of aes

pcol <- ggplot(data = mpg) + 
  geom_point(mapping = aes(x = displ, y = hwy, colour = class)) 


#AES Change Point size(size) by class or define size = 0 to 5 *outside of aes

psize <- ggplot(data = mpg) + 
  geom_point(mapping = aes(x = displ, y = hwy, size = class)) #not advised


#AES Change Point transparency (alpha) by class or name alpha = 0 to 1 *outside of aes

ptran <- ggplot(data = mpg) + 
  geom_point(mapping = aes(x = displ, y = hwy, alpha = class)) #not advised


#AES Change Point shape (shape  by class , or name shape = square *outside of aes)

pshp <- ggplot(data = mpg) + 
  geom_point(mapping = aes(x = displ, y = hwy, shape = class)) #best for <6 discrete values 


# Arrange into 2 rows and 2 columns
grid.arrange(pcol, psize, ptran, pshp, ncol = 2, nrow = 2)

```

AES Customization & Additional ggplot functions

```{r}

ggplot(data = mpg) + 
  geom_point(mapping = aes(x = displ, y = hwy, colour = class), shape = "triangle") +
  theme_classic() +
  labs(x = "display", y = "highway")

#adding numeric category 
ggplot(data = mpg) + 
  geom_point(mapping = aes(x = displ, y = hwy, colour = displ <5)) #all values <5 = TRUE
 
```

Facet and Panel plots

```{r}
# multiple plots in 1 "frame" e.g., ggplot facet_wrap *only for discrete variables

# for a single variable e.g., class use ##facet_warp
face1 <- ggplot(data = mpg) +
  geom_point(mapping = aes(x = displ, y = hwy), size = 0.7) +
  facet_wrap(~class, nrow = 2) #i.e., plot data for each class individually in 2 rows 

# for multiple variables e.g., drv ~ cyl use ##facet_grid
face2 <- ggplot(data = mpg) +
  geom_point(mapping = aes(x = displ, y = hwy), size = 0.7) +
  facet_grid(drv ~ cyl) 

# for non row/column dimensions use ##facet_grid(. ~ cyl)
face3 <- ggplot(data = mpg) +
  geom_point(mapping = aes(x = displ, y = hwy), size = 0.7) +
  facet_grid(. ~ cyl) #merges all hwy into single row 

#nrow/ ncol = defines number of rows/columns in plot
#labeller = label for each subset/plot

# Arrange into 2 rows and 2 columns
grid.arrange(face1, face2, face3, ncol = 2, nrow = 2)

```

Fitting Simple Lines

```{r}
 
ggplot(data = mpg) +
  geom_point(mapping = aes(x = displ, y = hwy), size = 0.7) +
  geom_smooth(mapping = aes(x = displ, y = hwy, linetype = drv, colour = drv)) 
#added line of best fit through scatter plot
#each line corresponds to class of drv

```

AES to categorical variable

```{r}

p1 <- ggplot(data = mpg) +
  geom_smooth(mapping = aes(x = displ, y = hwy)) #no grouping

p2 <- ggplot(data = mpg) +
  geom_smooth(mapping = aes(x = displ, y = hwy, group = drv)) #grouping, no colour diff

p3 <- ggplot(data = mpg) +
  geom_smooth(mapping = aes(x = displ, y = hwy, colour = drv), show.legend = FALSE) #group & colour diff

# Arrange into 2 rows and 2 columns
grid.arrange(p1, p2, p3, ncol = 2, nrow = 2)
```

Overarching mapping in base ggplot

```{r}

ggplot(data = mpg, mapping = aes(x = displ, y = hwy))+
  geom_point()+ #style points
  geom_smooth() #style lines
#this reduces duplication in code & errors when changing variables

ggplot(data = mpg, mapping = aes(x = displ, y = hwy))+
  geom_point(mapping = aes(colour = class))+
  geom_smooth(data = filter(mpg, class == "subcompact"), se = FALSE)+
  theme_classic()

#filter subset of data

```

Plotting Statistics

```{r}
library(ggplot2)
ggplot(data = diamonds) + 
  geom_bar(mapping = aes(x = cut)) #categorize cut based on levels

ggplot(data = diamonds) + 
  stat_count(mapping = aes(x = cut))
  
```

Overriding default in ggplot2

```{r}
library(tidyverse)

demo <- tribble(
  ~cut,         ~freq,
  "Fair",       1610,
  "Good",       4906,
  "Very Good",  12082,
  "Premium",    13791,
  "Ideal",      21551
)
demo #shows manual dataframe added 
  
ident <- ggplot(data = demo) +
  geom_bar(mapping = aes(x = cut, y = freq), stat = "identity") #plotted data


prop <- ggplot(data = diamonds) + 
  geom_bar(mapping = aes(x = cut, y = stat(prop), group = 1))
#bar chart for the proportion of total diamonds based on cut, group = 1 to treat all data as a single group


#Plotting Statistical Details 
#stat_summary() function to plot summary statistics (e.g., min, max, median) for a continuous variable (e.g., depth) across a categorical variable (e.g., cut)

stsum <- ggplot(data = diamonds) +
  stat_summary(mapping = aes(x = cut, y = depth), 
               fun.nmin = min, 
               fun.max = max, 
               fun = median)

# Arrange into 2 rows and 2 columns
grid.arrange(ident, prop, stsum, ncol = 2, nrow = 2)

```

Aesthetic adjustments Colour & fill adjustments

```{r}

fcut <- ggplot(data = diamonds) +
  geom_bar(mapping = aes(x = cut, fill = cut)) #fill colour based on cut

colcut <- ggplot(data = diamonds) + 
  geom_bar(mapping = aes(x = cut, colour = cut)) #outline colour based on cut

fclar <- ggplot(data = diamonds) + 
  geom_bar(mapping = aes(x = cut, fill = clarity)) #fill colour based on clarity

# Arrange into 2 rows and 2 columns
grid.arrange(fcut, colcut, fclar, ncol = 2, nrow = 2)

```

Positional adjustments e.g., identity,(raw data), fill(changes heights) and dodge(no staking) Position = "identity" (raw data overlapping i.e. stacking)

```{r}

#to alter transparency (alpha)
tclar <- ggplot(data = diamonds, mapping = aes(x = cut, fill = clarity))+
  geom_bar(alpha = 1/5, position = "identity") #raw data overlapping i.e. stacking

#to alter bar outlines w/ no fill
colclar <- ggplot(data = diamonds, mapping = aes (x = cut, colour = clarity))+
  geom_bar(fill = NA, position = "identity") #raw data overlapping i.e. stacking

# Arrange into 2 rows and 2 columns
grid.arrange(tclar, colclar, ncol = 2, nrow = 1)

```

```{r}
#Position = "fill" ####
#(standardize height of each bar to 1 i.e.,all bars same height)
#function: position = "fill" place each object exactly on graph, but standardize height of each bar to 1

posfill <- ggplot(data = diamonds)+
  geom_bar(mapping = aes(x = cut, fill = clarity), position = "fill") 


#Position = "dodge" ####
#(shows trends per category, place each object exactly on graph, but dodge bars next to each other)
#function = "dodge" place each object exactly on graph, but dodge bars next to each other

posdodge <- ggplot(data = diamonds)+
  geom_bar(mapping = aes(x = cut, fill = clarity), position = "dodge")


#Position = "jitter" ####
#(adds random noise to the location of each point to reduce over plotting)

posjit <- ggplot(data = mpg) +
  geom_point(mapping = aes(x = displ, y = hwy), position = "jitter")

#Arrange into 2 rows and 2 columns
grid.arrange(posfill, posdodge, posjit, ncol = 2, nrow = 2)

```

GGPLOT TEMPLATE

```{r}

#   ggplot(data = <DATA>) +
  #     <GEOM_FUNCTION>(mapping = aes(<MAPPINGS>), 
  #        stat = <STAT>, 
  #        position = <POSITION>) +
  #     <FACET_FUNCTION (wrap or grid> +
  #     <THEME_FUNCTION> +
  #     <LABS_FUNCTION>)

```
